# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (Sponsor)
**Source material:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has three AI use cases at different stages:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Client intends to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although that start date is not fixed.

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Four constraints shape the build:

* An approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* A requirement that customer data stays in the EU.
* A requirement that the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.
* Incumbent ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 management systems. The new AIMS must work alongside these systems rather than duplicate them.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Pure Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement can deliver a well-written set of governance documents. It cannot deliver a team that knows how to run them. Your objective requires governance that is operating, rather than documented, when visual inspection moves toward production.

In the Guided AI GRC Build, your team builds each artifact during weekly workshops and asynchronous work. Coaching sessions test and strengthen that work. This approach gives the Client three things:

1. **Ownership.** Your team understands why each control exists and can defend it.
2. **Retention.** The knowledge stays inside Tamarack Instruments after the program ends.
3. **Operating capability.** By Week 12, the Client runs its own reviews, assessments and evidence cycles.

The program is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. Each principle applies directly to visual inspection. Production decisions informed by AI need deliberate deployment, documented intent and a named human accountable for outcomes.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

The program uses the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Board-level reporting draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

**How the inventory is sequenced in Week 2:**

1. The customer service chatbot enters first because it is the only system recorded as deployed.
2. Visual inspection enters second because its Q2 2027 production target drives your objective.
3. Sales forecasting enters third as a planned system. This tests the intake process before the system is built.

Together these entries respond directly to the June 2026 audit finding.

**ISO/IEC 42001 readiness mapping.** Each week's artifacts are mapped to ISO/IEC 42001 readiness themes. These mappings indicate readiness only and are not a promise of certification.

**Integration with existing management systems.** The Profile Block names your ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 quality management system. It does not identify any specific register, procedure, control or record within them. For that reason, each integration point below is shown as `Unknown`. These points will be confirmed in Week 1 once the relevant artifacts are identified.

| Week | Tailored focus | Primary artifact | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Incumbent integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles; AIMS scope covering the three named use cases | Draft AIMS charter; mobilization brief | Context of the organization; leadership | Unknown |
| 2 | AI system inventory in the order above | Populated inventory | AIMS scope | Unknown |
| 3 | Classification against EU AI Act categories and GDPR considerations; risk methodology (classification outcomes: confirm with external counsel) | Classification record; risk methodology | Planning; risk criteria | Unknown |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments for the chatbot and visual inspection (relationship to GDPR data protection impact assessments: confirm with external counsel) | Completed assessments | AI risk assessment; AI system impact assessment | Unknown |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment plans | Operating risk register | Risk treatment | Unknown |
| 6 | Core policy set; mid-point steering | Adopted core policy set | AI policy; leadership commitment | Unknown |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance, including the pilot-to-production path for visual inspection | Lifecycle procedure | Operation; AI system lifecycle | Unknown |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance, including EU data residency checks; evidence collection begins | Supplier assessment criteria; evidence tracker | Third-party relationships; documented information | Unknown |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight using the Slow AI Kitchen, with a works council consultation step wherever a workflow touches production staff (confirm with external counsel) | Two governed workflow definitions | Operation; human oversight | Unknown |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring criteria for the inventoried systems | Monitoring plan | Performance evaluation | Unknown |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Incident and change procedures | Improvement; nonconformity and corrective action | Unknown |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Readiness review record; closing report | Internal audit and management review readiness | Unknown |

**Visual inspection timing.** The profile states that visual inspection is in pilot and does not say whether it touches production staff. If it does, the works council step applies before any change reaches the production line. That determination is `Unknown` and will be resolved in Week 1.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a functioning minimum viable AIMS. It consists of six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Open question on the second workflow.** The Profile Block identifies one deployed system, the customer service chatbot. Visual inspection is in pilot and targets production in Q2 2027, so it may not be in production use by Week 12. The second governed workflow is therefore `Unknown` at this stage. Selecting it is a required decision at the Week 1 steering checkpoint.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The build team is drawn from the roles you named: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. All figures below are estimates. They cover workshop attendance, coaching and asynchronous work. Actual effort will depend on the condition of existing documentation, which is currently `Unknown`.

| Role | Typical week (estimate, hours) | Peak weeks (estimate, hours) |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 | Weeks 1, 3, 6 and 12: 5 to 6 |
| CISO | 3 to 4 | Weeks 8 and 11: 5 to 6 |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 5 | Weeks 7 and 10: 6 to 8 |
| Head of Data | 4 to 5 | Weeks 2, 4 and 10: 6 to 8 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 | Weeks 7 and 9: 4 to 5 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 | Weeks 11 and 12: 4 |

**Internal auditor role.** We recommend the Client confirm how the two internal auditors take part in a way that preserves their independence. One option is an observing and challenge role, rather than authoring the controls they may later audit.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

* **Week 1** confirms scope, the build team, risks to delivery and the second governed workflow.
* **Week 6** reviews progress against the spine, open blockers and any scope decisions.
* **Week 12** reviews the minimum viable AIMS against its six elements and the 12-month operating plan.

Steering membership beyond the Sponsor is `Unknown` and should be confirmed before Week 1.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format and cadence.** Each week includes one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.

**Schedule.** Session times are `Unknown` and the start date is `Unknown`. A start in early January 2027 would complete the twelve weeks before Q2 2027. That timing should be confirmed against your production plan for visual inspection.

**Price.** The price for the Guided AI GRC Build is US$60,000. This falls within the approved budget of up to US$80,000 for this fiscal year. Invoicing terms and contract wording carry legal effect: confirm with external counsel.

## 8. Next Step

Before the 15 December 2026 decision date, we propose a short confirmation call with the Sponsor to settle five points:

1. The start date.
2. Steering membership.
3. Candidate systems for the second governed workflow.
4. The approach and timing for works council consultation.
5. Which ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 artifacts the AIMS should attach to.

On acceptance, Week 1 mobilization materials will be issued to the build team.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
